sentences.text: The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice T. Madhavi Devi

This writ petition is filed to declare the seizure of the petitioner's vehicle i.e., Ashok Leyland Goods Carriage LMV No.AP39-UH-6463 under the cover of panchanama dated 04.03.2024 in connection with Crime No.35 of 2024 of VM Banjar Police Station, Khammam District, as arbitrary and unconstitutional.

entities.text: VM Banjar Police Station, Khammam District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader for Civil Supplies appearing on behalf of respondents No.1 to 3 and learned Government Pleader for Home appearing on behalf of respondent No.4.
3.

The vehicle of the petitioner i.e., Ashok Leyland Goods Carriage LMV No.AP39-UH-6463 was seized under the cover of panchanama by respondent No.4 in connection with Crime No.35 of 2024 of VM Banjar Police TMD,J WP_31143_2024 Station, Khammam District, under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 7 and 8 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (for short 'the E.C. Act').
4.

entities.text: VM Banjar Police TMD,J WP_31143_2024 Station, Khammam District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Learned Government Pleader for Civil Supplies submitted that proceedings under Section 6-A of the E.C. Act, have been initiated against the petitioner and the same are pending.
Learned Government Pleader further submitted that the subject vehicle is still in the custody of respondent No.4-Police Station.

5. In view of the above facts and circumstances, taking into consideration the fact that the respondent authorities have initiated proceedings under Section 6- A of the E.C. Act and the same are pending, this Court is inclined to grant relief to the petitioner.

6. Accordingly, this Writ Petition is disposed of directing the respondent No.4-Station House Officer, VM Banjar Police Station, Khammam District, to release the vehicle i.e., Ashok Leyland Goods Carriage LMV No.AP39- TMD,J WP_31143_2024 UH-6463, under the cover of panchanama dated 04.03.2024 in connection with Crime No.35 of 2024 of VM Banjar Police Station, Khammam District, in favour of the petitioner subject to condition of his furnishing bank guarantee by way of Fixed Deposit for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) in favour of the 2nd respondent-District Collector (Civil Supplies), Khammam District.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This writ petition is filed to declare the seizure of the petitioner's vehicle i.e., Ashok Leyland Goods Carriage LMV No.AP39-UH-6463 under the cover of panchanama dated 04.03.2024 in connection with Crime No.35 of 2024 of VM Banjar Police Station, Khammam District, as arbitrary and unconstitutional.
The vehicle of the petitioner i.e., Ashok Leyland Goods Carriage LMV No.AP39-UH-6463 was seized under the cover of panchanama by respondent No.4 in connection with Crime No.35 of 2024 of VM Banjar Police TMD,J WP_31143_2024 Station, Khammam District, under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 7 and 8 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 (for short 'the E.C. Act').
4.
Learned Government Pleader for Civil Supplies submitted that proceedings under Section 6-A of the E.C. Act, have been initiated against the petitioner and the same are pending.
Learned Government Pleader further submitted that the subject vehicle is still in the custody of respondent No.4-Police Station.
opennyai_summary.decision:
5. In view of the above facts and circumstances, taking into consideration the fact that the respondent authorities have initiated proceedings under Section 6- A of the E.C. Act and the same are pending, this Court is inclined to grant relief to the petitioner.
6. Accordingly, this Writ Petition is disposed of directing the respondent No.4-Station House Officer, VM Banjar Police Station, Khammam District, to release the vehicle i.e., Ashok Leyland Goods Carriage LMV No.AP39- TMD,J WP_31143_2024 UH-6463, under the cover of panchanama dated 04.03.2024 in connection with Crime No.35 of 2024 of VM Banjar Police Station, Khammam District, in favour of the petitioner subject to condition of his furnishing bank guarantee by way of Fixed Deposit for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) in favour of the 2nd respondent-District Collector (Civil Supplies), Khammam District.
Release of the vehicle shall be subject to outcome of the confiscation proceedings under Section 6-A of the EC Act.
Pending such proceedings, the petitioner is directed not to alienate or alter physical features of the subject vehicle,
and is further directed to produce the vehicle as and when required by the authorities concerned.
No order as to costs.
1 Miscellaneous applications, if any, pending in this writ petition, shall stand closed.
